section: Divorce / The Little Children and Jesus

heading.en: What God joined, and who Jesus welcomed

body.en: Pharisees tested Jesus, asking if divorce was lawful. Jesus pointed back to creation: 'God made them male and female... a man will be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh. So they are no longer two, but one. What God has joined together, let no one separate.' Moses permitted divorce because of hardened hearts, but that was never God's original design for marriage. Later, people brought little children to Jesus for Him to touch, but the disciples rebuked them — children weren't considered important enough to bother Jesus! Jesus was INDIGNANT and said: 'Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these. Truly I tell you, anyone who will not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.' Then He took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them, and blessed them. Jesus didn't just tolerate children being brought to Him — He was upset that anyone tried to keep them away.

verse.en: Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

title.en: A Song for Let the Children Come

q.en: What did Jesus point back to, when asked about divorce?

en: God's original design at creation — one flesh, joined together

q.en: How did the disciples initially react when people brought children to Jesus?

en: They rebuked the people, trying to keep children away

q.en: How did Jesus feel about the disciples trying to keep children away?

en: Indignant — upset that they tried to hinder the children

label.en: Activity sheet: Let the Children Come

body.en:
Big idea: Jesus' strong, visible emotion ("indignant") at the disciples' attempt to keep children away reveals how highly He values them — not as an afterthought, but as a living picture of the humble, trusting receptivity the kingdom of God actually requires. The marriage teaching grounds lasting covenant commitment in God's original creation design, not merely cultural or legal convention.

Conversation starters: (1) Why might Jesus get genuinely upset, not just mildly correct the disciples, about keeping children away? (2) What does it mean to "receive the kingdom like a little child" — what qualities does a child have that adults can lose? (3) How does God's original design for marriage as "one flesh" shape how we think about commitment?

Pray, thanking Jesus for how much He values children, and asking for childlike trust in Him.
